clue.text: Remind actor to be punctual

blocks.note: first meaning: to feed a forgotten line to a performer
second meaning: on time, without delay

explanation.surface: A stage manager nags a performer about turning up on time.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for cueing a performer's forgotten line and an adjective for arriving exactly on schedule.

clue.text: Inhaling one, smoker becomes more bloated

indicators.note: inhaling means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a smoker puffs on a cigarette
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A smoker who takes in another cigarette swells up.
explanation.definitionFit: Puffy means swollen, so the comparative describes something more swollen or bloated.

clue.text: Switch positions without consistency

blocks.note: first meaning: the two settings of a simple switch
second meaning: intermittent, as in an on-and-off relationship

explanation.walkthrough: 'Switch positions' sounds like swapping places, but it names the two settings of a light switch.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-setting switch has these states, and something intermittent or erratic is also described this way.

clue.text: One is responsible for gripping pages

definitions.text: One is responsible for gripping pages

blocks.clueFragment: One is responsible for gripping pages
blocks.note: surface reading: an author who writes a page-turner
setter's reading: physically holding sheets of paper together

explanation.walkthrough: 'Gripping' suggests an exciting book; it is literal, a small wire clasp holding sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: This bent wire office item clamps several sheets together, literally holding onto them.

clue.text: Tasteless dip is in preparation

indicators.note: something in preparation is being mixed and made up, so the letters are being reworked

blocks.note: taken as written, seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A cook admits the dip being made for the party has no flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: Insipid food lacks flavour, so it is a direct synonym for bland or tasteless.

clue.text: Provisional team I am to join

blocks.note: Inter Milan, the Italian football club
contracted as I'm

explanation.surface: A player says they will sign for a club on a temporary deal.
explanation.definitionFit: An interim arrangement is temporary, in place only until a permanent one is made.

clue.text: Auction includes hard rock

indicators.note: includes means holds within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: an auction is a sale
H for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An auction lot features some hard rock music memorabilia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard rock' reads as a music genre, but hard gives one letter and rock alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Shale is a fine-grained sedimentary rock that splits into thin layers.

clue.text: I have many gods, a nature one above all?

blocks.note: Pan is the Greek god of nature and the wild
above all others is 'the 1st', with the digit 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A worshipper of many deities wonders if a nature god outranks the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads 'Pan the 1st': the nature god as the first above all others.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantheism identifies God with the universe, and many pantheists accept or tolerate worship of numerous deities.

clue.text: Daughter at cathedral city losing some energy: nothing sinister about this

indicators.note: losing some means part of the supply is lost, so one of the matching letters goes

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
Exeter, the cathedral city in Devon
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A daughter living in a cathedral city is tired but harmless.
explanation.walkthrough: Exeter has two E's after the X; only one is lost, which is why the clue says 'some'.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry dexter is the right side and sinister the left, so dexter is the opposite of sinister.

clue.text: Hit gym for exercise to get strong

indicators.note: exercise means moving about, so the letters are put through a workout into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trainer's advice: go to the gym and work out to build strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Mighty means powerful, a direct synonym for strong.

clue.text: Mark that shows one has passed

definitions.text: Mark that shows one has passed

blocks.clueFragment: Mark that shows one has passed
blocks.note: surface reading: an exam result showing a pass
setter's reading: passed means walked by, leaving an impression of a sole in the ground

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' and 'passed' suggest an exam grade; the passing is literal walking, and the mark is left in mud or sand.
explanation.definitionFit: The impression left on the ground by a walker's shoe is evidence that someone went by that way.

clue.text: Appropriate evidence from ballot paper one has voted for princess?

blocks.note: Princess Anne, the British Princess Royal

blocks.clueFragment: evidence from ballot paper one has voted
blocks.note: the cross a voter marks on the ballot paper

explanation.surface: A cross on a ballot paper proves the voter backed the princess.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads X for Anne, so the princess comes first and the cross follows. 'Appropriate' is the verb, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To annex territory is to seize it for oneself, which is what appropriate means as a verb.

clue.text: Conclude wearing mink will be picked up

indicators.note: picking up a sound means hearing it, so what counts is how the phrase is said

blocks.note: someone wearing mink is dressed in fur

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that a lady in a mink coat will be collected by a chauffeur.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to reach a conclusion by reasoning from evidence, the verb sense of conclude.

clue.text: Bit of luck perhaps after finding this on the hoof

definitions.text: Bit of luck perhaps after finding this on the hoof

blocks.clueFragment: Bit of luck perhaps after finding this on the hoof
blocks.note: surface reading: a stroke of fortune met in passing, 'on the hoof' meaning casually
setter's reading: the thing literally sits on a hoof and is a traditional lucky charm

explanation.walkthrough: 'On the hoof' is an idiom for doing something without planning; here it is literal, the iron nailed under a hoof, which is also hung up for luck.
explanation.definitionFit: The U-shaped iron fitted to a hoof is a well-known good-luck token, so finding one is lucky.

clue.text: Such a wealthy family unlikely to be Republicans?

definitions.text: Such a wealthy family unlikely to be Republicans?

blocks.clueFragment: Such a wealthy family unlikely to be Republicans?
blocks.note: surface reading: a rich American dynasty and its party politics
setter's reading: republicans want no monarch, so a ruling family would hardly be among them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Republicans' suggests the US party; read as opponents of monarchy, the family is the reigning one.
explanation.definitionFit: Kings, queens and their relatives form a rich family that obviously would not want monarchy abolished.

clue.text: What to do for new baby? Anything

definitions.text: What to do for new baby?

blocks.clueFragment: What to do for new baby?
blocks.note: first meaning: an instruction to the parents to choose a name
second meaning: the phrase for whatever you care to mention

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is read literally as an order to give the baby a name, and idiomatically as 'whatever you like'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom offers an open list of possibilities, meaning any item at all.

clue.text: Page I'm to edit, a flyer in black and white

definitions.text: a flyer in black and white

indicators.note: editing text changes and rearranges it, so the letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: An editor has a black-and-white advertising leaflet to work on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' looks like a printed leaflet, fitting page and edit, but it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The magpie is a bird with distinctive pied plumage, so a black and white flier.

clue.text: Grand Eastern terminus in development?

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
E for eastern
a terminus is the end station of a line

explanation.surface: A grand railway terminus in the east is being redeveloped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand Eastern terminus' sounds like the name of a station, but it splits into three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Gestation is the period of growth of a baby in the womb, or figuratively of an idea.

clue.text: After massage on back go for physical exercise

indicators.note: going back means running the other way, so the word is read from its end
says the second piece comes after the first in the answer

blocks.note: to massage is to rub
to go, informally, is to urinate

explanation.surface: A physiotherapist, having massaged a patient's back, sends them off for a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' in the bathroom sense is a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A burpee is a squat-thrust exercise combining a squat, plank and jump, used in fitness workouts.

clue.text: Struggling, hence an upgrade needed

indicators.note: something struggling is in disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A failing business concludes it must improve.
explanation.definitionFit: To enhance something is to improve its quality, the verb sense of upgrade.

clue.text: Content indicator has husband horribly aghast

indicators.note: something done horribly is badly messed up, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: H is the standard abbreviation for husband
taken as written

explanation.surface: A husband is horrified by what some label on a social post shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' looks like part of the wordplay, but only H and the six letters of aghast are shuffled; 'has' joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: On social media a word after the # symbol labels what a post is about, flagging its topic.

clue.text: Hound is down regularly in this bay

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: first, third, fifth and so on of these letters

explanation.surface: A dog lies down every so often on the shore of a bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hound' hints at baying dogs, but the bay is a body of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Hudson Bay is the vast inland sea in northern Canada.

clue.text: Rather like Marx to be bad-tempered

blocks.note: first meaning: resembling Groucho Marx, the comedian
second meaning: grumpy and irritable

explanation.walkthrough: Marx suggests Karl, but it is Groucho, one of the Marx Brothers; the word adds -y to his name.
explanation.definitionFit: A grouchy person is irritable and complaining, a synonym for bad-tempered.

clue.text: Townsman drops hot snack

indicators.note: drops means lets fall away, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: a burgher is a citizen of a town
H for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A townsman lets his warm snack fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A burger is a minced-meat patty in a bun, a common fast-food snack.

clue.text: Brazen, say, you steal an outhouse

indicators.note: say asks for the spoken form of the next word, which is a single letter sound

blocks.note: the letter U is pronounced like the word you
to nab is to snatch or steal
an outhouse is a shed

explanation.surface: Someone shamelessly accuses another of pinching a garden building.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unabashed feels no embarrassment, which is the shameless boldness that brazen describes.

clue.text: Looking for roof-beam to be shortened at one end

indicators.text: to be shortened at one end
indicators.note: shortening at one end trims the word, here dropping the first letter

blocks.note: a rafter is a sloping roof timber

explanation.surface: A builder searches for a roof timber that needs trimming.
explanation.definitionFit: To be after something is to seek it, as in 'he's after a job', meaning looking for.

clue.text: Somewhat inappropriate to buy on this

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the next word is used, a run of letters inside it

blocks.note: the letters run from the third to the seventh of this word

explanation.surface: Someone says it is a bit unsuitable to purchase under these terms.
explanation.walkthrough: Buying 'on appro' (short for approval) means taking goods home with the right to return them.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'on appro' describes a trial purchase, so it is the arrangement one buys on.

clue.text: Contemptuous expression putting pressure on playwright

blocks.note: P is the symbol for pressure
George Bernard Shaw, the Irish dramatist

explanation.surface: A critic scoffs while pressuring a dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: Pshaw is an old-fashioned interjection voicing impatience or disdain.

clue.text: Grey with worry that's serious

blocks.note: GR is a dictionary abbreviation for grey
to eat someone is to worry them, as in what's eating you

explanation.surface: A person going grey from anxiety has a grave problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Great can mean considerable or significant, as in great danger, a sense shared with serious.

clue.text: From an earlier age one has moved into Chile

indicators.note: moved means shifted about, so the letters change places

blocks.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An immigrant from an older generation has settled in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one has moved into' reads as a single migration, but the fodder is just 'into Chile'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Neolithic period is the New Stone Age, a prehistoric era long before recorded history.

clue.text: One out of work on Scottish island

blocks.note: re means on or concerning
Tiree is an island in the Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: An unemployed person is living on a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: A pensioner who has stopped working for good is no longer in employment.

clue.text: A particular method to make such a mirror

definitions.note: the answer is the kind of mirror, used as an adjective

blocks.note: first meaning: a single way of doing something
second meaning: a mirror that is a window from one side only

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is two words, a single approach; the second is the hyphenated adjective, as in police interview rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-way mirror reflects on one side but can be seen through from the other, as in interrogation rooms.
